data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the policy for secure remote access to United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) information and information systems prior to, during, and upon return from foreign locations.
policy_statements.target: United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) information and information systems

policy_statements.source_text: It is USDA policy to comply with Federal requirements to establish, implement, and enforce a policy on:
USDA information systems that facilitate remote access from international locations; and
policy_statements.target: USDA information systems that facilitate remote access from international locations

policy_statements.source_text: The use of devices and removable media when used to remotely access USDA information systems from international locations.
policy_statements.target: use of devices and removable media

policy_statements.source_text: This policy complies with the requirements of:
The Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA);
cross_references: The Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA)

cross_references: OMB, M-17-12, Preparing for and Responding to a Breach of Personally Identifiable Information

policy_statements.source_text: Telework Enhancement Act of 2010.

policy_statements.source_text: This policy serves as the foundation for agencies and staff offices to develop and implement foreign remote access policies and procedures that comply with Federal and Departmental requirements.
This policy applies to:

All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, and others who work for, or on behalf of, USDA and use, or are responsible for, maintaining USDA information systems remotely accessed by devices or use removable media from international locations; and
policy_statements.target: All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, and others who work for, or on behalf of, USDA and use, or are responsible for, maintaining USDA information systems remotely accessed by devices or use removable media from international locations

policy_statements.source_text: All Federal information, in any medium or form, generated, collected, provided, transmitted, stored, maintained, or accessed by, or on behalf of, USDA and all information systems or services (including cloud-based services) used or operated by USDA, USDA contractors, or other organizations on behalf of, or funded by, USDA.
policy_statements.target: All Federal information, in any medium or form, generated, collected, provided, transmitted, stored, maintained, or accessed by, or on behalf of, USDA and all information systems or services (including cloud-based services) used or operated by USDA, USDA contractors, or other organizations on behalf of, or funded by, USDA

policy_statements.source_text: This directive builds on other information security policies that cover application and client device security requirements used domestically.
However, this DR is written with an emphasis on specifying requirements for ensuring the security of USDA information systems when individuals remotely access them from foreign locations.
Related policies include:
DR 3505-003, Access Control for Information and Information Systems, forthcoming;
cross_references: DR 3505-003, Access Control for Information and Information Systems, forthcoming

policy_statements.source_text: DR 3580-004, Securing Remote Access to USDA Information Systems and Client Devices, November 30, 2018; and
cross_references: DR 3580-004, Securing Remote Access to USDA Information Systems and Client Devices, November 30, 2018

policy_statements.source_text: DR 35xx-xxx, Bring Your Own Device, forthcoming.
cross_references: DR 35xx-xxx, Bring Your Own Device, forthcoming

policy_statements.source_text: Users should comply with DR 5400-007, Text Messaging While Driving, which provides safety guidance about the use of Government furnished equipment while driving.
policy_statements.target: DR 5400-007, Text Messaging While Driving
cross_references: DR 5400-007, Text Messaging While Driving

policy_statements.source_text: Nothing in this policy will alter the requirements of DR 4080-811-002, Telework Program, that defines approved worksites for USDA, when those worksites may be used, and the conditions in which they may be used.
cross_references: DR 4080-811-002, Telework Program

policy_statements.source_text: Nothing in this policy will alter the requirements for the protection of information associated with national security systems such as those identified in FISMA, policies, directives, instructions, and standards issued by the Committee on National Security Systems (CNSS), or the intelligence community.
cross_references: FISMA

policy_statements.source_text: This policy is effective immediately and remains in effect until superseded.
conditions: until superseded

policy_statements.source_text: All agencies and staff offices will align their international remote access policies and procedures with this policy within 6 months of the publication date.
policy_statements.target: international remote access policies and procedures
conditions: within 6 months of the publication date

policy_statements.source_text: This DR uses the term “remote client device” in place of NIST’s “telework client device.”
The two categories of client devices used in this policy and defined by NIST are:
Personal computers (PC) (e.g., desktops and laptops); and
Mobile devices (e.g., smartphones, tablets).
Note: The term “remote client device” in this DR encompasses any device in the two categories of devices used to remotely access USDA information systems.
USDA desktop computers within USDA facilities that access USDA information systems do not need the same security requirements as remote client devices that access USDA information systems remotely.
Section 5a addresses USDA desktop requirements when they remotely access USDA facilities.

The term “controlled unclassified information” (CUI) replaces and encompasses all previous terms and labels for sensitive information such as for official use only (FOUO), sensitive but unclassified (SBU), Sensitive Security Information (SSI), and personally identifiable information (PII).
The categories of CUI can be found in the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) CUI Registry – Categories and Subcategories.
cross_references: National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) CUI Registry – Categories and Subcategories

policy_statements.source_text: The term “burner” refers to a client device that cannot be sanitized to meet NIST SP 800-88 Revision 1, Guidelines for Media Sanitization requirements and is to be used once; the primary use is during foreign travel to a country of high risk .
cross_references: NIST SP 800-88 Revision 1, Guidelines for Media Sanitization

policy_statements.source_text: The term “Government furnished” followed by “equipment,” “device,” or their plural forms will be used to describe the category of devices whose security posture is managed by USDA.
The term is used in place of “Organization-Controlled Device,” which NIST uses and is defined in Appendix B.

The terms “international travel” and “foreign travel” apply to trips, as well as permanent duty assignments in any country, territory, or commonwealth outside of the United States and its territories.

The term “wireless” refers to client devices, (e.g., laptops, mobile devices) and networking devices (e.g., access points) exchanging data through radio communication within a limited geographic area, such as an office building.
Wi-Fi is a trademark of the Wi-Fi Alliance.
The USDA remote access infrastructure affords personnel convenient and efficient methods to use USDA resources from external locations.
policy_statements.target: personnel

policy_statements.source_text: However, remote client devices used to perform work from foreign locations introduce additional risks to USDA information and information systems; therefore, these devices have additional security requirements than those operating within USDA controlled areas and those operating from remote locations within the United States and its territories.

System owners that permit access to information systems from foreign locations must safeguard USDA information systems from threats arising from the lack of physical security controls, the use of insecure networks, and potentially compromised client devices used by personnel on foreign travel.
policy_statements.target: USDA information systems
conditions: that permit access to information systems from foreign locations

policy_statements.source_text: Personnel using remote client devices are responsible for protecting them by knowing when, where, and how the devices are permitted to be used.
policy_statements.target: remote client devices

policy_statements.source_text: Foreign governments are very skilled at collecting information even from devices that are turned off.
Devices and sensitive information taken to foreign countries are susceptible to infection and compromise.
Infected devices may not be discovered upon return and, if reconnected to USDA networks, may compromise the security of additional information.
For these reasons, the Department strongly discourages personnel from taking devices to foreign countries.
policy_statements.target: personnel

policy_statements.source_text: Personnel should be mindful of restrictions on electronic equipment that may be brought aboard aircraft and that the restrictions may change without notice.
The Department of Homeland Security and, potentially, the Department of State websites may have updated information about restrictions on electronic equipment.

Employees can obtain security and threat briefings prior to traveling by following the guidance below and, when on travel with an official U.S. passport, by scheduling a security and threat briefing at a U.S. Embassy or Consulate.
policy_statements.target: security and threat briefings
conditions: prior to traveling
when on travel with an official U.S. passport

policy_statements.source_text: Government furnished desktop computers, when used remotely from international locations to access or store USDA information, will have the same information storage, configuration, operational, and sanitization requirements as laptops in this DR.
policy_statements.target: Government furnished desktop computers
conditions: when used remotely from international locations to access or store USDA information

policy_statements.source_text: International travel locations identified as “a country of high risk” are based on:
The ISSPM, based on information about the traveler’s destination in the Department of State Travel Advisories or Travel to High-Risk Areas web pages;
cross_references: Department of State Travel Advisories
Travel to High-Risk Areas

policy_statements.source_text: Information provided by the ASOD Threat Intelligence team; and
Information provided by Office of Homeland Security (OHS) Personnel and Document Security Division (PDSD).
Agencies and staff offices whose personnel travel to a country of high risk will have a process with OHS PDSD to obtain a high-risk travel briefing.
conditions: whose personnel travel to a country of high risk

policy_statements.source_text: Personnel with security clearances will request a high-risk travel briefing by sending an email to pdsd@dm.usda.gov; and
policy_statements.target: high-risk travel briefing

policy_statements.source_text: All other personnel will use the OHS Foreign Travel Information web page.
policy_statements.target: OHS Foreign Travel Information web page
cross_references: OHS Foreign Travel Information

policy_statements.source_text: Additional responsibilities and duties described in Departmental Manual (DM) 3440-001, USDA Classified National Security Information Program Manual, apply to Information Security Coordinators (ISC) and to personnel with national security clearances traveling internationally.
cross_references: Departmental Manual (DM) 3440-001, USDA Classified National Security Information Program Manual

policy_statements.source_text: Agencies and staff offices will ensure their personnel have international travel security and threat awareness information that reflects current and relevant changes to the threat environment for the traveler’s foreign destinations and includes but is not limited to:
Unclassified threat information obtained from the Department of State’s Travel Advisories and Travel to High-Risk Areas web pages;
cross_references: Department of State’s Travel Advisories
Travel to High-Risk Areas

policy_statements.source_text: Cybersecurity and physical threats in the foreign countries;
The cybersecurity controls required for remote client devices that will be used during international travel;
Requirements for physical protection of remote client devices and removable media contained in this policy;
Requirements for protection of CUI, including restrictions on printing;
Prohibited use of public wireless networks in foreign countries; and
Restricted use of Bluetooth in foreign countries.

Agencies and staff offices will provide a fully patched, securely configured USDA wireless router to personnel whose international permanent duty station is outside of a U.S. Embassy, consulate, or other U.S. Federal building.
policy_statements.target: fully patched, securely configured USDA wireless router
conditions: whose international permanent duty station is outside of a U.S. Embassy, consulate, or other U.S. Federal building

policy_statements.source_text: The routers will include the following settings:
Enable Wi-Fi Protected Access 2, often displayed as “WPA2/Enterprise;”
Disable Wi-Fi Protected Setup; and
Enable strong shared key.

Agencies and staff offices will use diplomatic pouches to deliver Government furnished devices and removable media to personnel whose permanent duty station is in a foreign location or when countries prohibit travelers from hand carrying electronic devices while traveling.
policy_statements.target: Government furnished devices and removable media
conditions: whose permanent duty station is in a foreign location
when countries prohibit travelers from hand carrying electronic devices while traveling

policy_statements.source_text: Government furnished remote client devices and removable media used domestically will only be taken on international travel when:
Supporting USDA business functions;
The USDA employee has obtained approval from their supervisor; or
For contract support staff, the contractor has obtained approval from the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR); and
When a waiver has been submitted and approved.
An approved waiver will be required to take government furnished remote client devices and removable media to a country of high risk.
policy_statements.target: government furnished remote client devices and removable media

policy_statements.source_text: Personnel whose BYOD or third-party-controlled mobile device is provisioned in USDA’s BYOD program will follow the requirements in DR 35xx-xxx, Bring Your Own Device, prior to and upon return from international travel.
policy_statements.target: requirements in DR 35xx-xxx, Bring Your Own Device
conditions: whose BYOD or third-party-controlled mobile device is provisioned in USDA’s BYOD program
prior to and upon return from international travel
cross_references: DR 35xx-xxx, Bring Your Own Device

policy_statements.source_text: Agencies and staff offices that permit client devices to be taken outside the United States will:
conditions: that permit client devices to be taken outside the United States

policy_statements.source_text: Maintain an inventory of loaner and burner client devices and basic cell phones (non-smartphones with only voice and text capability) to be issued and used during international travel, or have an alternate process to harden Government furnished remote client devices used domestically and authorized for use on foreign travel;
policy_statements.target: inventory of loaner and burner client devices and basic cell phones (non-smartphones with only voice and text capability)

policy_statements.source_text: Assess the risk of bringing such devices and removable media into the foreign country, including the risks of theft, confiscation, breach of data confidentiality and integrity, communications intercept, the insertion of malware into the devices, and unsuccessful sanitization;
policy_statements.target: risk of bringing such devices and removable media into the foreign country

policy_statements.source_text: Have procedures to:
Assess the threat capabilities in the traveler’s destinations using threat intelligence from the ASOD’s threat intelligence team and, when necessary, their agency or staff office ISC or OHS PDSD;
conditions: when necessary
policy_statements.target: threat capabilities in the traveler’s destinations

policy_statements.source_text: Contact ASOD, 30 days in advance of travel via email to the cyberthreat@asoc.usda.gov mailbox to determine whether a country to be visited is a country of high risk.
conditions: 30 days in advance of travel

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure the devices are appropriately configured based on the threat intelligence about the foreign destination prior to being taken on international travel; and
policy_statements.target: devices

policy_statements.source_text: Arrange shipment of Government furnished devices and removable media via diplomatic pouch with U.S. Embassies or U.S. consulates.
policy_statements.target: shipment of Government furnished devices and removable media

policy_statements.source_text: Configure such devices to meet domestic security controls plus the following international travel requirements:
Ensure basic cell phones only have voice and text capabilities;
policy_statements.target: basic cell phones

policy_statements.source_text: Disable Bluetooth and wireless networking services, and instruct the user on how to enable these services when needed and disable them again when not needed;
conditions: when needed
when not needed

policy_statements.source_text: Instruct users to conduct remote client device data communications to USDA information systems over cellular networks using a Virtual Private Network (VPN);
policy_statements.target: users

policy_statements.source_text: Enroll mobile devices into a Mobile Device Management (MDM) solution, and add the provisioning profile that establishes an encrypted container;

a. This policy applies to:
(1) All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, and others who work for, or on behalf of, USDA and use, or are responsible for, maintaining USDA information systems remotely accessed by devices or use removable media from international locations; and
(2) All Federal information, in any medium or form, generated, collected, provided, transmitted, stored, maintained, or accessed by, or on behalf of, USDA and all information systems or services (including cloud-based services) used or operated by USDA, USDA contractors, or other organizations on behalf of, or funded by, USDA.
b. This directive builds on other information security policies that cover application and client device security requirements used domestically. However, this DR is written with an emphasis on specifying requirements for ensuring the security of USDA information systems when individuals remotely access them from foreign locations. Related policies include:
(1) DR 3505-003, Access Control for Information and Information Systems, forthcoming;
(2) DR 3580-004, Securing Remote Access to USDA Information Systems and Client Devices, November 30, 2018; and
(3) DR 35xx-xxx, Bring Your Own Device, forthcoming.
c. Users should comply with DR 5400-007, Text Messaging While Driving, which provides safety guidance about the use of Government furnished equipment while driving.
d. Nothing in this policy will alter the requirements of DR 4080-811-002, Telework Program, that defines approved worksites for USDA, when those worksites may be used, and the conditions in which they may be used.
e. Nothing in this policy will alter the requirements for the protection of information associated with national security systems such as those identified in FISMA, policies, directives, instructions, and standards issued by the Committee on National Security Systems (CNSS), or the intelligence community.

The USDA remote access infrastructure affords personnel convenient and efficient methods to use USDA resources from external locations.

However, remote client devices used to perform work from foreign locations introduce additional risks to USDA information and information systems; therefore, these devices have additional security requirements than those operating within USDA controlled areas and those operating from remote locations within the United States and its territories.

System owners that permit access to information systems from foreign locations must safeguard USDA information systems from threats arising from the lack of physical security controls, the use of insecure networks, and potentially compromised client devices used by personnel on foreign travel.
that permit access to information systems from foreign locations
Personnel using remote client devices are responsible for protecting them by knowing when, where, and how the devices are permitted to be used.
Foreign governments are very skilled at collecting information even from devices that are turned off.
Devices and sensitive information taken to foreign countries are susceptible to infection and compromise.
Infected devices may not be discovered upon return and, if reconnected to USDA networks, may compromise the security of additional information.
For these reasons, the Department strongly discourages personnel from taking devices to foreign countries.
Personnel should be mindful of restrictions on electronic equipment that may be brought aboard aircraft and that the restrictions may change without notice.
The Department of Homeland Security and, potentially, the Department of State websites may have updated information about restrictions on electronic equipment.
